newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae aims for 15 pct EPS growth rate.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae aims for 15 pct EPS growth rate.

text.p: Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) said Friday a business plan filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) as part of its proxy statement projects a minimum commpound annual growth rate in earnings per share of 15 per cent over the next five years.
Sallie Mae said it will schedule a shareholder meeting on the first Thursday 20 days after completing the SEC Review. Sallie Mae said it anticipates the meeting would take place in mid-July.

In a news release, David Vitale, vice chairman of Sallie Mae and designated in the proxy filing as the non-executive chairman of Sallie Mae, said the business plan calls for maximizing student loan revenue through expansion of a campus-based strategy.

Sallie Mae is a government-sponsored enterprise which buys student loans from lenders and securitizes them in the capital markets. The company is seeking to privatize and end its government link. Vitale said the plan also seeks to significantly lower operating expenses. Another element of the plan is to aggressively manage capital, primarily through loan securitizations and common share repurchases, Vitale said.
Vitale said the plan also calls for investment in servicing and client-support systems and minimization of political risk.

Vitale asserted that the business plan of an opposition group called the Committee to Restore Value (CRV) is risky and has already cost Sallie Mae lost business. "We have lost a substantial volume of student loan purchases in the last two months as a result of the CRV's publicly declared intention to originate student loans in head-to-head competition with our principal business suppliers," he said.
In an interview earlier in the week, Vitale cited estimates that the lost business amounted to $250 million.
